historical_record.description: The building went up as Stick-Eastlake flats on the north side of Post Street between Laguna and Buchanan, before 1893 — it appears on the area's earliest Sanborn map; the architect is unknown.
A permit was issued for a one-storey addition built out into the front setback, to hold a billiard parlour and a barber shop; it stayed until 1978.
The Nippon Drug Company was trading from the storefront, and stayed through the 1930s and into the early 1940s.
The Nippon Drug Company and the two men who ran it were gone from the building, the year Japanese Americans were forced into incarceration.
By 1950 the building belonged to Charles Sullivan, the Black businessman and property owner who also owned the Fillmore Auditorium.
James "Jimbo" Edwards opened a waffle-and-chicken restaurant in the storefront, with the owner paying his first three months' rent; it became Jimbo's Waffle Shop, and then Jimbo's Bop City.

About four months after the restaurant opened, the back room became an after-hours jazz club: a bandstand and piano went in, admission was a dollar (free with an instrument), and it was named after New York's Bop City.
Jimbo's Bop City closed, as rock displaced jazz and redevelopment emptied the surrounding Fillmore; the storefront then became Soko Hardware and later its storeroom.
One of the buildings moved to the Victorian Village development at Sutter and Fillmore in the late 1970s — the former Jimbo's Bop City club from 1690 Post Street — and now home to Marcus Books.
Before moving the building, the Redevelopment Agency tore off the one-storey storefront addition that had stood in the front setback since 1910.
The building was moved three blocks from Post Street, where the Japantown mall was going up, after the activist Essie Collins of the Western Addition Community Organization petitioned to save it.

Marcus Books moved into this Victorian-era house in 1980 and stayed for more than three decades, until the owners lost the property to foreclosure in 2013 and the business was evicted the following year. The house had stood at 1690 Post Street, where it held the jazz club Jimbo's Bop City in the 1950s and early 1960s, before being moved here as part of the Victorian Square redevelopment project.
Julian Richardson and his wife bought the building from the Redevelopment Agency to bring Marcus Books back to the Fillmore.
Designated a San Francisco landmark in 2014.

unknowns: Built about 1893 on its original Post Street site, though the assessor gives 1880.

notable_residents.name: Slim Gaillard
notable_residents.detail: The jazz musician Slim Gaillard rented the ground-floor restaurant space in the late 1940s, before leaving for Los Angeles.

notable_residents.name: James "Jimbo" Edwards
notable_residents.detail: James "Jimbo" Edwards ran Jimbo's Bop City in this building until 1965, an integrated 2-to-6 a.m. club where Miles Davis, Dizzy Gillespie, Charlie Parker, John Coltrane, Ella Fitzgerald and Billie Holiday played.

notable_residents.name: Julian Richardson
notable_residents.detail: Julian Richardson, founder of Success Printing and of Marcus Books and a co-founder of Fillmore groups that pushed back against redevelopment, lived in the flat above the store until his death in 2000.
